title: AI Deal Frenzy Powers Hong Kong Fundraising to Record Summer
source_used: Bloomberg (syndicated text read on The Edge Malaysia)
key_facts: Hong Kong IPOs, placements and block trades raised US$47.5 billion in July to September 2026, the biggest third quarter on record, per data compiled by Bloomberg.
Fundraising in Hong Kong this year is above US$92 billion, within reach of the US$112.5 billion record set in 2021.
Alibaba's US$10.2 billion follow-on offering was the biggest deal of the quarter; Zhongji Innolight raised almost US$8 billion in Hong Kong's largest listing in nearly seven years.

AI model maker Z.AI has raised US$9.6 billion this year through its IPO, placements and convertible bonds; MiniMax, Iluvatar CoreX and Biren also returned to the market in July soon after their IPO lockups expired.
Asia-Pacific share sales topped US$120 billion in the quarter, the most for the period in six years; India had a record US$26 billion quarter.
The boom came despite a sell-off: the MSCI Asia-Pacific Index fell as much as 7% in July, and rising bond yields and weak deal performance are making investors more cautious.
quote_evidence: Initial public offerings, placements and block trades raised US$47.5 billion (RM194 billion) in July-September, the biggest haul ever for the period, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.
"People raise capital right out of lockup and tend to do so more frequently," said James Wang, head of Asia ex-Japan equity capital markets at Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

That pushed fundraising this year above US$92 billion and within reach of the US$112.5 billion record set in 2021, though the recent surge in bond yields and poor deal performance are making investors and issuers more cautious.
why_it_matters_hint: Chinese AI companies are tapping Hong Kong investors repeatedly and in record sums, even as the stock market itself falls.
event_date: Quarter ended 30 Sep 2026; article dated 4 Oct 2026
